correctness.rationale: The prior invariant-Bezoutian criterion is used only set-theoretically: degree six has no prime-Dickson exception, so only the two nontrivial composition orders occur. Once the inner factor is monic with constant zero, vanishing of the sextic t⁵ coefficient centers the inner factor. Centering the outer factor instead is possible by an intermediate translation, which does not change the composite or its coefficient image. The coefficient expansions give a dense h=1 open of the plane and of the scroll, respectively. Independently, the rank-one locus of the displayed matrix is the Segre hyperplane xz₁=yz₂; over [x:y] its fibers are the projectivized kernel of O³→O(1) with coefficients x,−y,0. The kernel splits as O(−1)⊕O, hence a smooth irreducible cubic scroll. Set J=(Q₁,Q₂), F=A²−4hC. The displayed syzygies expand to BF and DF. For any f∈(B,D)∩(J,F), write f=j+sF; since F is not a zero divisor modulo (B,D), s∈(B,D), so sF∈J. This directly proves equality of J with the intersection of the prime ideals and confirms height two and the reduced closure. The sum of the ideals gives the smooth conic in the plane. On h=1, elimination gives B(4C−A²)=0, and at the sole boundary point of the conic the chart C=1 gives D(A²−4h)=0. The two factors are independent local coordinates in each chart, giving the completed normal crossing and the singular ideal of the conic (the two node coordinates). The conic is reduced as the scheme intersection, giving generic multiplicity one along it; this is not a claim about a proper intersection number of the surfaces in ambient P⁴. Outside the conic a single smooth component is present. The Koszul Hilbert series simplifies to (1+z)²/(1−z)³, giving the claimed polynomial and degree, and CI adjunction gives ω_R=O_R(−1); the section polynomial 4n gives genus one. These are exact algebraic checks; the frozen checker was read but not executed.
